citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
APHIS officials observed one male rabbit with hair loss and matting on approximately 50 percent of its tail. The underside
of the tail contained dried brown material. Yellowish brown staining, focal hair loss, and matting were observed on the
back legs and feet as well. This animal was observed with a hunched posture and its ears pushed back, which are both
suggestive of pain. Additionally, this animal was reluctant to move when APHIS officials approached. These signs may
indicate an underlying disease process that requires prompt veterinary care and were not communicated to the attending
veterinarian prior to the inspection. The facility must inform the attending veterinarian of this animal's condition and follow
their guidance by August 21, 2026.
Additionally, the following was observed in all 10 rabbits and constitutes a noncritical non-compliant item.
There were small focal areas of hair loss on the ears and back of the rabbits, which were dispersed in a random pattern.
Some of the underlying skin appeared to be thickened. According to a facility representative, this condition was observed
approximately one week ago but was not communicated to the attending veterinarian. This condition must be
communicated to the attending veterinarian by August 24, 2026.

APHIS officials observed a loose board on a ramp leading up to a walking bridge in an enclosure housing 17 goats.
Additionally, APHIS officials observed a board pried loose off of a fence with screws sticking straight up in an enclosure
housing 16 sheep and 1 llama, which was removed by a facility representative at the time of the inspection. These issues
have the potential to cause injury to the animals. The facility must ensure that the indoor and outdoor housing facilities are
structurally sound and maintained in good repair to protect the animals from injury and to contain the animals. To be
corrected by August 27, 2026.

APHIS officials observed an excessive accumulation of feces and food waste in an enclosure housing 17 goats. The
excrement and food waste were attracting flies, which were too numerous to count. Excessive accumulation of feces and
food waste can attract pests and transmit disease to the animals. The facility must ensure that animal and food wastes
are removed to minimize vermin infestation, odors, and disease hazards. To be corrected by August 27, 2026.

APHIS officials observed 1 peafowl in an enclosure without sufficient shelter. Although there was a partial roof, all sides
were exposed to the elements. Insufficient shelter can expose birds to discomfort. The facility must ensure that the shelter
comfortably contain all the birds at one time and prevent their discomfort from the elements. To be corrected by
September 3, 2026.

citations.desc: Cleaning, sanitization, housekeeping, and pest control.
citations.narrative:
APHIS officials observed a chicken coop with approximately 2 inches of excrement and other waste covering the floor of
the coop, which housed 15 chickens. A build up of excrement and waste can cause disease and attract pests. The facility
is required to remove excrement and waste as often as necessary to prevent excessive accumulation. To be corrected by
August 27, 2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with facility representatives.
Additional Inspectors:
Tomeka Manson, VETERINARY MEDICAL OFFICER n
